gen.title: Understanding population definitions and genetic variation

cards.stem: How does research describe racial classifications for explaining human genetic variation?
options: Research has demonstrated that racial classifications are inadequate descriptors
Research proves racial groupings perfectly predict allele frequencies
Research shows race provides complete explanations for human variation
Research confirms racial categories are definitive measures of difference
cards.quote: Research has demonstrated that racial classifications are inadequate descriptors of the distribution of genetic variation in the human species

cards.stem: What characteristic defines a population in the biological sense?
options: In biology, a population generally denotes a group
A random collection of individuals with no shared breeding pattern
A collection of different species coexisting in one habitat
All organisms worldwide that carry a specific allele
cards.quote: In biology, a population generally denotes a group whose members breed primarily or solely among themselves

cards.stem: What mistaken idea is described about human populations and race?
options: A common misconception is that human populations fall into uniform groups
A proven fact is that human groups show complete genetic uniformity
Accurate research shows races have distinct and separate gene pools
Established pattern is that ethnicity fully explains genetic traits
cards.quote: A common misconception is that human populations fall into uniform groups with large biological differences, which lie along racial boundaries

cards.stem: What alternative grouping is mentioned for classifying the human species?
options: An alternative to classifying the human species by race
The only way to define populations is by geographic isolation
Physical isolation is required for any breeding to occur
Self-described ethnicity always matches familial origins exactly
cards.quote: An alternative to classifying the human species by race is to divide them by ethnicity
